lines.en: Six legs take turns on the wet ground.

lines.zh: 尾桨在水面上划开一道
lines.en: My tail paddle cuts a line on the water.
I walk slowly along the shallows.
My forelimbs push the duckweed aside.
Six legs make a dense rhythm.
Belly low, I move along the water.
My prints come in three pairs.
I swing my tail and turn for the bank.
The water only reaches my belly.
I test each step before taking it.
Four legs brace, the rear two push.
Water weeds slide between my legs.
I circle the bend of the river.
A line of my back shows above water.
My sixth leg is the strongest.
I head for where the fish are.
I lie in the shallows, still.
All six legs rest on the sand.
The water reflects my long snout.
I open my jaws, then close them.
Bubbles rise by my jaw.
I hold still as a rotten log.

lines.zh: 阳光在背上留了一小块暖
lines.en: A patch of sun warms my back.
My eyes sit high on my head.
I lift my head slightly to breathe.
My snout rests on the sand.

lines.zh: 水草缠了我的腿,我不理
lines.en: Weeds cling to a leg; I ignore them.
This bend of the river is quiet.
I dip to the bottom and rise again.
Six shadows of legs on the riverbed.
I wait for the current to cool.
This spot is comfortable.
My long snout turns to you.
You stepped into my water.
Half of me is under water.
You cannot tell how long I am.
I surface only to look at you.
My eyes are on top of my head.
The bank is slippery there.
None of my six legs moved.
Do you mean to come into the water?
The water has begun to ripple.
I slowly shift aside.
In the water, I am faster than you.
I slide into the water to soften it.
A scale has been torn off.
My six legs lose their rhythm.
I flick my tail and pull back.
I sink half my body.
This body does not take hits well.
I gape once to breathe.

lines.zh: 我的血混进泥水，味道发腥。
lines.en: My blood mixes into the mud; it smells rank.
I can still swim.
I swim toward the depths.
There is a smell of blood in the water.
I swing my tail toward the scent.
This smell is very fresh.
What you hold is dripping.
I work my jaws open once.
I follow along the bank.
My six legs speed up underwater.
The smell in the mud: a little closer.
I am not fussy; edible is enough.
Lower your hand.
My snout is already aimed.
That smells better than river fish.
I push half my body out.
Wait; the water will help me.

lines.zh: 我伏在泥里，等你再走两步。
lines.en: I lie in the mud, waiting for two more steps.
That ought to be mine.
You struck my back.
I slide half a foot.
A body like mine does not take hits well.
The water pushed me back.

lines.zh: 尾鳍被你踩进泥里，抽不出来。
lines.en: You pin my tail in the mud; I cannot pull it free.
My whole body twists.
Two pairs of my legs scramble.
I retreat back into the water.
In the water, I have the advantage.
Do not crowd me on land.
We float side by side.
I bring my snout close.

lines.zh: 水底的沙被我们搅起来
lines.en: We stir the sand beneath us.

lines.zh: 我的六条腿轻轻碰你的
lines.en: My six legs brush yours.
This shallows is quiet enough.

lines.zh: 我们一起沉下去又浮上来
lines.en: We sink together and rise again.

lines.zh: 水流会把我们的味道带走
lines.en: The current will carry our scent.

lines.zh: 不用说话,水会替我们说
lines.en: No words; the water speaks for us.
Swim ahead; I follow.
This bend is ours.
I take it in my jaws at once.
It slid down my throat.
I found it on the riverbed.
I cannot eat this.
I spit it out and take it again.
I pin it with a forelimb.
It sinks in water.
Hard, but no matter.
I bury it in the sand.
I will keep it to eat later.
The current has given you away.
You are completely fixed in my sight.
I am faster beneath the surface.
You stand on the bank; perfect.
I flatten myself lower.
I can reach from here.
I open my jaws and hold.
This bank is too narrow.
I see your feet in the mud.
I sink slowly.
I follow you beneath the surface.
Only a ripple shows on the surface.
I am right downstream of you.
I move only when you look away.
Six legs, and I walk steady.
The water is only to your knee.

lines.zh: 我的牙齿排得整整齐齐。
lines.en: My teeth line up in neat rows.
My tail sweeps below.
There is no one else here.
The water will move for me first.
My long jaws snap shut.
I lunge up out of the water.
This bite can lock on an ankle.

lines.zh: 平牙咬住，我把你往泥里按。
lines.en: Flat teeth bite; I press you into the mud.
Six legs brace against the bottom.
My teeth are fine and many.
I roll and twist.
The surface bursts apart.
Your boots are too heavy to drag.
I retreat into deeper water.

lines.zh: 河底的沙一鼓，我露出背脊。
lines.en: The riverbed sand swells; my back breaks the surface.

lines.zh: 六条腿一条条撑起身体
lines.en: My six legs lift me one by one.
My snout breaks the surface first.
My tail paddle muddies the water.
I surface, eyes above water.
Three pairs of prints on the shallows.

lines.zh: 我从淤泥里抬头，甩落水珠。
lines.en: I lift my head from the silt and shake off drops.
My sixth foot settles last.
See those two lines on the water?
Those two lines are me.
The water heats; I leap up.

lines.zh: 我摔在河岸上,弹了两下
lines.en: I hit the bank and bounce twice.

lines.zh: 我在水里,却吸不到空气
lines.en: In the water, yet I cannot breathe.
The water erupts and flips me.

lines.zh: 一根尖东西扎进我的背
lines.en: Something sharp pierces my back.

lines.zh: 那股力量让我的鳞立起来
lines.en: That force raises all my scales.
Too hungry to swing my tail.

lines.zh: 雷打进水里,我全身一僵
lines.en: Lightning hits the water and I lock up.
There is not even water here.
